topic: Neural Network Learning and Intuitive Backpropagation

sections.title: The Big Picture: Learning via Trial and Error
lecture_lines: Neural networks learn through trial and error.
Every learning process starts with a simple guess.
We check results and fix our mistakes.
animations: Archer #FFFFFF and target #FFFFFF appear on screen.
Archer shoots arrow #FFFF00; it misses high on target.
Red #FF0000 bracket measures distance from bullseye to arrow.
Archer tilts body downward to adjust for the miss.
Archer shoots again; arrow #00FF00 hits the center bullseye.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Neuron
lecture_lines: Neurons receive inputs and apply adjustable weights.
Weights decide which input features matter most.
Biases help fine-tune the final decision.
animations: Two circles #FFFFFF (Inputs) labeled "Color" and "Shape".
Lines (Weights) connect inputs to a central neuron circle.
A "Bias" knob [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/kn.svg] #AAAAAA adds a constant to the neuron.

sections.title: The Forward Pass: Making a Guess
lecture_lines: Information flows forward through layers of neurons.
Each neuron calculates a weighted sum of inputs.
This sum passes through an activation function.
The network produces a final prediction.
We compare this prediction to the ground truth.
animations: Input values 0.8 and 0.2 enter the input circles.
Multiplication signs appear on weight lines as data flows.
Summation symbol #00FFFF glows inside the central neuron.
An 'S' shaped Sigmoid gate #FFFFFF filters the output.
Final prediction value 0.7 appears at the network exit.

sections.title: The Loss Function: Measuring the 'Ouch'
lecture_lines: Loss measures the distance between guess and reality.
High loss indicates a very inaccurate prediction.
We want to minimize this error value.
animations: Prediction 0.7 and Truth 1.0 appear on a line.
The gap 0.3 is highlighted with red #FF0000 color.
A square box #FF5555 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg] representing (0.3^2) Loss appears.

sections.title: Backpropagation: The Chain of Blame
lecture_lines: Backpropagation traces error backwards through the network.
We assign blame to every weight and bias.
The chain rule calculates each parameter's error contribution.
Gradients show the direction of maximum error increase.
This tells us how to fix our mistakes.
animations: Red glow #FF0000 starts at the prediction output.
The glow moves backward through the Sigmoid gate.
The "Error" signal splits to trace back through weights.
Each weight knob [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knob.svg] #FFFF00 flashes indicating its "Blame" level.
Calculated gradients appear next to each adjustable weight knob [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knob.svg].

sections.title: Gradient Descent: Nudging the Knobs
lecture_lines: Gradient descent nudges weights to reduce loss.
We move weights opposite to the gradient direction.
The learning rate determines our step size.
We descend toward the point of minimum error.
The network optimizes itself one step at a time.
animations: A ball [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] #00FF00 sits on a hilly Cost Landscape curve.
The ball [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] rolls down one step toward the bottom.
Weight knobs [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/knob.svg] turn slightly based on the descent step.

sections.title: Summary: The Iterative Loop
lecture_lines: Learning is a loop of guessing and correcting.
Each iteration makes the network more accurate.
Repetition creates intelligence from simple adjustments.
animations: Icons for Forward, Loss, Backprop, and Descent form a loop.
The Archer shoots a sequence of arrows hitting bullseye.
A "Model Trained" checkmark #00FF00 appears in the center.
